title.narrative: Social and affordable housing support programme for Kosovo

description.narrative: As a leading multilateral institution promoting inclusive and sustainable spatial planning in the Western Balkans region, UN-Habitat gives attention to effectively using the means of implementation for the 2030 Agenda, especially in the area of sustainable urban development. UN-Habitat Kosovo supports ministries and municipalities in providing effective local governance and spatial planning responses, sustainable urban mobility, housing, cultural heritage, environmental protection, public space development, and improvement of urban conditions for all residents. UN-Habitat in Kosovo has become a regional leader in supporting strategic municipal planning and people’s engagement designed to make municipalities more inclusive and sustainable, notably through its’ flagship ‘Inclusive Development Programme, financed by Swedish Development Cooperation. In addition, UN-Habitat has supported the Kosovo Government, respectively the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure (Department of Planning, Construction and Housing) to conduct feasibility study for a sustainable social housing programe in Kosovo with two main components: Kosovo-wide assessment report on social housing needs (Output 1) and Elaboration of social housing programme concept for Kosovo (Output 2). This study was supported with funding from the Italian Fund for Innovative Projects (IFIP) received through the Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB). In course of this support and in responding to the priorities set out by MESPI, UN-Habitat Kosovo will continue its support towards the implementation phase of the Adequate Social Housing Programme for Kosovo (3 pillars). In January, MESPI concluded the Feasibility Study on Adequate Social Housing for Kosovo. This study was implemented by UN-Habitat Kosovo and financed by CEB (Council of Europe Development Bank) through the Italian Fund for Innovative Projects, and was endorsed by all relevant stakeholders (MESPI, MRC, MIA, MFA, MLGA, MoFLT). The proposed programme is composed by three main pillars: 1) Adequate Social Housing, 2) Adequate Neighbourhoods, and 3) Adequate Home Improvement, while the study provides a detailed roadmap for establishment of a sustainable social and affordable housing system in the Kosovo. In addition, a complementary part of this study is a comprehensive matrix with specific activities, housing interventions gathered around four (4) main levels: Community level, institutional capacity building, policy level, and housing market level. Following this, in November 2022, CEB Bank approved €25 million loan to Kosovo that will finance the first phase of a comprehensive “Adequate Social Housing Programme” aiming to establish a long-term sustainable social and affordable housing system in the country and improve living conditions of marginalised and low-to-middle-income households. The loan is given for the first phase, covers only 2 pillars (Adequate Social Housing and Adequate Home Improvements), and about 2,000 households will benefit from these investments. In addition, MESPI has applied to WBIF for technical assistance support grant (2 million EUR), which will cover some of the activities foreseen in the phase 1 (results will be announced next year, March-April 2023). But, considering the volume of preparatory activities required for starting the implementation (phase 1) of this programme (building the proper housing system, developing the housing pillars and other related activities), there is a need for: an intensive local-central dialogue, coordination with local and international stakeholders (CEB, WBIF), knowledge sharing, international expertise and very good managements skills for all these interdisciplinary and complex processes. In this regard, the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure has expressed interest in cooperating with UN-Habitat, as an intermediate interlocutor between all relevant stakeholders, and a technical assistance provider during the implementation of activities related to the main components (see the Table 2) derived from the feasibility study (concept proposal). UN-Habitat’s long-time support to MESPI, worldwide experience, and ongoing role in facilitating such dialogue and processes will positively impact the development and implementation of programme activities in this regard. Therefore, this cooperation will be an extension of activities within the cooperation framework between UN-Habitat Kosovo and MESPI, which aims to achieve the objectives derived from the Feasibility Study. This Project Document outlines activities and expected results for Phase 1 (2025–2029) of a broader programme aimed at supporting social and affordable housing in Kosovo. While additional phases may be considered in the future, this document covers only the currently funded phase.
